subject: Post-demo: litmus plan, recommended models, and parity acceptance
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@luminaryhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: litmus plan, recommended models, and parity acceptance

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth while your team finishes internal alignment: 

1) What we heard
- Primary goal: replace current proprietary reranker for patient-sentiment routing with an open-model-based stack while matching or exceeding the baseline's precision@10.
- Success criteria: parity at segment-level (precision/recall) and no more than 5% degradation in per-message latency at peak QPS.
- Constraints: must run within Luminary's existing cloud region (us-west), and procurement will prefer single-vendor SLA for inference.

2) Redwood recommended starting kit (what we can ship for a litmus test):
- Models to trial: gpt-open-light-13B-quant (fast variant), redwood-regen-7B (higher-precision variant) — both available with our Dedicated or Private options.
- Prompt set: attached prompt-set-v2.txt (includes reranking prompts, temperature settings, and hard-negative examples).
- Benchmarks: lightweight benchmark run (summary attached) that mirrors your sample traffic.

3) Parity proposal and acceptance thresholds (initial)
- Precision@10 >= baseline_precision - 2 percentage points
- Macro F1 on labeled clinical intent >= baseline - 3 percentage points
- Tail-latency (95th) <= baseline + 50ms at test QPS

4) Next steps
- We’ll deliver the parity matrix (attached) and an annotated prompt set by EOD tomorrow.
- If the thresholds look acceptable, propose a 2-week litmus test on a shadowed path with traffic mirroring.
- Procurement: please share any vendor questionnaire pointers (security, data residency) and we’ll loop CS/Compliance.

Attachments: parity-matrix-v1.xlsx, prompt-set-v2.txt, benchmark-run3-summary.html

If that aligns, I’ll put a short technical deep-dive on the calendar with Rishi and Marissa for Wed.

Thanks —
Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
pri.yom@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@luminaryhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <pri.yom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luminary Procurement <procurement@luminaryhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: litmus plan, recommended models, and parity acceptance

Thanks Priyom — that recap is helpful. A few quick notes from our side: 

- The success criteria are roughly right. For internal stakeholders the single biggest ask is that we don't regress on clinical intent F1 on the NER/routing classes that we've labeled "critical" (about 18% of traffic). Can you add a target specifically for that segment?
- Procurement asked for a simple SOW outline and a copy of SOC2 docs before we schedule any pilot. Can your team share the standard SOW template and SOC2 artifact?
- We're open to a 2-week shadow test but will need real-time monitoring hooks (token-level latency, per-request model variant) and a clear rollback plan. 

I'll get procurement to review the attachments and get back with specific questionnaire items.

Best,
Alex
Principal PM, Luminary Health
alex.chen@luminaryhealth.com

Adding a few concrete items we can own from the motion side: 

- I'll prepare the parity-matrix-v1.xlsx with the additional "critical segment" row Alex requested and include a column for per-class sample counts and confidence bands. ETA: tomorrow 11:00am PT.
- Rishi, recommend we include a fallback policy: if the open model drops below parity on the critical segment for 3 consecutive days in the litmus window, traffic should automatically fall back to the proprietary reranker for affected intents. I can add that as an operational step in the playbook.
- Procurement ask: I have our standard SOW template and SOC2 redacted artifact; I'll attach to the HubSpot deal and send a link.

Small ask to Alex: can Luminary share a 3k-message anonymized sample for the critical segment so we can run a more targeted run? If not, a small stratified sample will do.

—Marissa

From: Priyom Das <pri.yom@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: litmus plan, recommended models, and parity acceptance

Alex — quick follow with the artifacts and a slightly tightened acceptance table (attached in parity-matrix-v1.xlsx):

- Critical-segment F1 >= baseline - 1.5 percentage points
- Precision@10 (global) >= baseline - 2 percentage points
- 95th-latency delta <= baseline + 40ms at test QPS

I've uploaded the SOW + SOC2 stub to the HubSpot record and linked the sample benchmark run (run-20270110-3) so you can see the exact traffic mix we used. Link: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/runs/run-20270110-3

Prompt notes: the prompt-set-v2.txt includes a conservative reranker prompt and explicit negative sampling for the critical intents. We found that adding a short calibration step (3-shot with in-domain hard negatives) reduces false positives by ~8% on our runs.

Action items I own:
- Send calendar invite for technical deep-dive (Rishi, Marissa, Alex + Luminary eng) — proposed Wed 10:00am PT.
- Run targeted critical-segment pass once Alex shares the sample (Marissa will pick up the run).
- Provide SOW + SOC2 artifacts to procurement (done, link in HubSpot).

If that sounds good I'll lock the Wednesday slot and request the sample.

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <pri.yom@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@luminaryhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: litmus plan, recommended models, and parity acceptance

Quick operational note before the deep-dive: 

- Fallback policy: we'll implement a per-intent circuit-breaker based on a rolling 24h F1 window; threshold = critical-segment F1 < (baseline - 1.5pp) for two consecutive evaluation windows. That triggers routing to the proprietary reranker and an automated alert to Luminary + Redwood runbook.
- Monitoring hooks: token-level latency, model-variant tag, per-intent F1, and sample-extraction (store 1% of decisions for audit). We'll provide Grafana dashboards and a small Prometheus exporter for metrics.
- Scheduling: Wed 13 Jan 2027 10:00am PT accepted — Alex, please confirm and I'll send the invite.

Rishi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
